speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; can you tell me exactly what activities trigger these symptoms, such as feeding, crying, or lying down? Also, has anyone noticed if the breathing sounds worse when you lie on your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia.

The symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, along with post-prandial vomiting, are classic for this condition; do you have any information on whether the symptoms improve when the infant is held in a prone or supine position versus sitting upright?
